gloss: think, plan, devise; reckon, count, impute; regard, esteem; design (skilled work)
summary: To work a thing out in the mind: to plan or devise, to count and calculate, to reckon a thing as something or to someone's account, to regard or esteem, and, of the tabernacle's craftsmen, to design skilled woven and metal work. Its noun מַחֲשָׁבָה is a thought or plan, of men's hearts, which Yahweh knows to be vapour, and of Yahweh's own heart, which stand for ever; חֶשְׁבּוֹן is a reckoning, of which there is none in the grave. The verb is the word of Gen 15:6, “he reckoned it to him as righteousness”, which Paul expounds in Romans 4 with the Peshitta's same verb. Arabic ḥasaba “count, reckon” and ḥasiba “think, suppose”, and the Aramaic and Syriac verb, cover the same ground.

words.gloss: plan, devise; reckon, count as, impute; regard, esteem; design; calculate, consider
words.summary: About a hundred and twenty times, in four stems. Its core is reckoning in the mind: working out a plan, counting up a sum, setting a thing down as something or to someone's account. The qal plans and reckons; the niphal is to be reckoned or regarded; the piel calculates and considers; the participle חֹשֵׁב is the designer of the tabernacle's woven work.

stems.gloss: plan, devise, intend; reckon as, take for; reckon to, impute; regard, esteem; design

senses.definition: To work out in the mind what one will do, usually against someone, for evil or for good; of men and of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “You planned (חֲשַׁבְתֶּם) evil against me; God planned it (חֲשָׁבָהּ) for good, to keep many people alive.”
“Woe to those who devise iniquity and work evil on their beds; in the morning light they do it”: the plan made in the night is carried out by day.
“Behold, I am forming (יוֹצֵר) evil against you and devising (חֹשֵׁב) a plan against you”: parallel to the potter's forming.
Assyria “does not intend (יְדַמֶּה) so, nor does his heart plan (יַחְשֹׁב) so; for it is in his heart to destroy”.
Haman “had devised against the Jews to destroy them”.
Saul “planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines”.
Sanballat and Geshem “were planning to do me harm”.
Gog, coming up against the regathered land of unwalled villages: “things will come into your heart, and you will devise an evil plan”.
“Let none of you devise evil in your heart against his neighbour.”
“Yahweh purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; he stretched out a line.”
“The thoughts that I think (חֹשֵׁב) toward you … thoughts of peace and not of evil.”
Those “who devise evil things in their heart”.
“Do you plan to reprove words?”

senses.gloss: reckon as, take for, consider to be
senses.definition: With לְ or כְּ: to count a person or thing as something it is taken to be, rightly or wrongly.

evidence.note: “Judah saw her וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לְזוֹנָה, for she had covered her face”: he took her for a harlot.
Hannah's lips moved but her voice was not heard, “and Eli took her (וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ) for a drunken woman”.
“Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?”
“He counts me to himself as his adversaries.”
“My maids count me as a stranger.”
Leviathan “counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood”.
“Do you count this as justice?”
“We counted him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.”

senses.gloss: reckon to, set to one's account, impute
senses.definition: With לְ of the person: to set something down to someone's account, as righteousness, or as iniquity.

evidence.note: “He believed in Yahweh, וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה”: he reckoned it to him as righteousness.
“Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity (לֹא יַחְשֹׁב … לוֹ עָוֺן).”
Shimei: “Let not my lord reckon iniquity to me, and do not remember what your servant did wrongly”: parallel to “remember”.
Paul quotes Gen 15:6; the Peshitta's verb is the same root (וֵאתֿחַשבַּתֿ).
Paul quotes Psa 32:2; Peshitta נֵחשֻובֿ.

senses.definition: To count a person or thing as of worth, to have regard for it; with a negative, to set no value on it.

evidence.note: The Medes “do not regard silver, and gold they do not delight in”: parallel to חָפֵץ.
“He was despised, and we did not esteem him (לֹא חֲשַׁבְנֻהוּ).”
A book of remembrance was written “for those who fear Yahweh and for those who esteem his name (וּלְחֹשְׁבֵי שְׁמוֹ)”.
“He has broken the covenant, despised the cities, he regards no man.”
“I am poor and needy; Adonai thinks on me (יַחֲשָׁב לִי).”

senses.gloss: design, devise skilled work; (participle) designer, skilled weaver
senses.definition: To devise artistic work in gold, silver, bronze, stone, wood and woven stuff; the participle חֹשֵׁב is the craftsman who designs and weaves patterned cloth, “the work of a designer” being the tabernacle's finest weaving.

evidence.note: Bezalel is filled with the spirit of God “to devise designs (לַחְשֹׁב מַחֲשָׁבֹת), to work in gold, in silver and in bronze”.
“The work of a craftsman (חָרָשׁ) and of a designer (חֹשֵׁב) and of an embroiderer … and of a weaver (אֹרֵג), doers of every work and devisers of designs (חֹשְׁבֵי מַחֲשָׁבֹת)”.
The curtains of the dwelling, “cherubim, the work of a designer (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב)”.
The ephod, “the work of a designer”.
Oholiab, “a craftsman and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and purple”.
Huram-abi, skilled “to devise every design (וְלַחְשֹׁב כָּל־מַחֲשָׁבֶת)”.
Uzziah's engines, “the invention of an inventor (מַחֲשֶׁבֶת חוֹשֵׁב)”.
“Like David they devise for themselves instruments of song.”

stems.gloss: be reckoned to; be reckoned as, regarded as; be accounted of worth

senses.gloss: be reckoned to, set to one's account
senses.definition: With לְ of the person: of an offering, a gift or a deed, to be credited or charged to someone.

evidence.note: Peace offering eaten on the third day: “it will not be accepted; it will not be reckoned (לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב) to him who offers it”.
“Blood will be reckoned to that man; he has shed blood.”
“Your contribution will be reckoned to you as the grain of the threshing floor.”
Phinehas's act: “it was reckoned (וַתֵּחָשֶׁב) to him as righteousness to all generations for ever”, the words of Gen 15:6.
A loud blessing early in the morning “will be reckoned to him as a curse”.

senses.gloss: be reckoned as, regarded as, counted
senses.definition: With כְּ or לְ: to be counted as or among something, or as like it.

evidence.note: Rachel and Leah: “Are we not regarded by him as foreigners? For he has sold us.”
“The nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are reckoned as dust on the scales.”
“I am reckoned with those who go down to the pit.”
“We are reckoned as sheep for slaughter”, quoted in Rom 8:36 (Peshitta וֵאתֿחשֵבֿנ).
“All the nations are as nothing before him; they are reckoned by him as less than nothing.”
“They also are reckoned as Rephaim, like the Anakim.”
Unwalled village houses “shall be reckoned as the field of the land”.
“Shall the potter be reckoned as the clay?”
“The great things of my law are reckoned as a strange thing.”
“Even a fool who keeps silent is reckoned wise.”
The precious sons of Zion “reckoned as earthen jars”.
“They were reckoned faithful.”

senses.gloss: be accounted of worth; be accounted for
senses.definition: To be counted as anything, to have value; and of money handed over, to be reckoned up.

evidence.note: “Silver was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.”
“Cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for at what is he to be reckoned?”
“No reckoning shall be made with them (לֹא־יֵחָשֵׁב אִתָּם) of the silver given into their hand, for they deal faithfully.”

stems.gloss: calculate, reckon up; think on, consider; devise; be about to

senses.definition: To count up years or money to settle what is owed, in the law of redemption and valuation, and in accounts with workmen.

evidence.note: “He shall calculate the years of its sale and return the excess.”
The redeemed slave “shall calculate with his buyer from the year he sold himself to the year of jubilee”.
“The priest shall calculate for him the amount of your valuation until the year of jubilee.”
“They did not reckon with the men into whose hand they gave the silver, for they dealt faithfully.”

senses.definition: To turn a matter over in the mind: past days, one's ways, a trouble, or man himself.

evidence.note: “I considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.”
“I thought on my ways, and turned my feet to your testimonies.”
“Yahweh, what is man that you know him, the son of man that you think on him (וַתְּחַשְּׁבֵהוּ)?” parallel to יָדַע.
“When I thought how to understand this, it was trouble in my eyes.”

senses.definition: As the qal: to plan a course, often evil.

evidence.note: “A man's heart plans his way, but Yahweh establishes his step.”
“He who plans to do evil will be called a master of schemes.”
“I strengthened their arms, yet against me they devise evil.”
“What do you devise against Yahweh?”

senses.definition: Once, of a ship in a storm: to be on the point of something, as though it reckoned on it.

evidence.note: “The ship thought to be broken (חִשְּׁבָה לְהִשָּׁבֵר)”: was about to break up.

senses.definition: Once: to count oneself as one of a number.

evidence.note: Balaam of Israel: “Behold, a people dwelling alone, and not reckoning itself among the nations.”

evidence.locator: Gen.15.6, וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ → ἐλογίσθη; Psa.32.2, יַחְשֹׁב → λογίσηται; Psa.44.23, נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ → ἐλογίσθημεν; λογίζομαι and its forms render חָשַׁב about fifty times

evidence.note: “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned (ἐλογίσθη) to him for righteousness”: Gen 15:6.
“Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not reckon (λογίσηται) sin”: Psa 32:2.
“We were reckoned (ἐλογίσθημεν) as sheep for slaughter”: Psa 44:23.
“Not reckoning (μὴ λογιζόμενος) their trespasses to them”: the language of Psa 32:2.

parallels.note: “Form, fashion”: Yahweh forms evil and devises a plan, as the potter forms the clay.
“Intend, think”: Assyria's heart did not so intend nor so plan.
Not to reckon iniquity is not to remember it.
To know man and to think on him.

phrases.gloss: reckon it to him as righteousness
the work of a designer (patterned weaving)

words.gloss: thought; plan, purpose, device; design (artistic work)
words.summary: Fifty-six times, most often plural, with the construct מַחֲשֶׁבֶת. What the heart works out: thoughts, plans and purposes, of men and of Yahweh; and in Exodus and Chronicles the designs of skilled craftsmen, as the verb's participle is the designer.

senses.definition: What goes on in a man's heart, known to Yahweh: in scripture most often evil, and to be forsaken.

evidence.note: “Every form of the thoughts of his heart (יֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ) was only evil all the day.”
“Yahweh knows the thoughts of man, that they are vapour (הֶבֶל)”, quoted in 1Co 3:20.
“Yahweh searches all hearts and understands every form of the thoughts.”
“Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts, and return to Yahweh”: parallel to דֶּרֶךְ.
“Wash your heart from evil … how long will your thoughts of iniquity lodge within you?”
“Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity.”
A rebellious people “who walk in a way not good, after their own thoughts”.
“Thoughts of evil are an abomination to Yahweh.”

senses.definition: A plan worked out to be carried out: men's plans and schemes, often against others, and Yahweh's purposes, which stand.

evidence.note: “I know the thoughts that I think toward you … thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope.”
“The counsel of Yahweh stands for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations”: parallel to עֵצָה.
“Many are the plans in a man's heart, but the counsel of Yahweh, that will stand.”
“Plans fail without counsel, but with many advisers they stand.”
“My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways my ways.”
The nations “do not know the thoughts of Yahweh, nor understand his counsel”.
“You have seen all their vengeance, all their plans against me.”
Haman's “plan that he had devised against the Jews”.

senses.definition: The designs of skilled craftsmen in metal, stone, wood and cloth; and once a contrivance of war.

evidence.note: “To devise designs (מַחֲשָׁבֹת), to work in gold, in silver and in bronze.”
“To make every work of design (מְלֶאכֶת מַחֲשָׁבֶת).”

evidence.locator: Psa.94.11, מַחְשְׁבוֹת → διαλογισμούς; διαλογισμός renders מַחֲשָׁבָה ×9

evidence.note: “The Lord knows the reasonings (διαλογισμούς) of the wise, that they are futile”: Psa 94:11.
“Out of the heart come evil thoughts (διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί)”; Peshitta מַחשבָֿתָֿא בִּישָתָֿא.

evidence.locator: Jer.29.11, מַחְשְׁבוֹת → λογισμόν; λογισμός renders מַחֲשָׁבָה about fifteen times

evidence.note: “Casting down reasonings (λογισμούς)”; Peshitta מַחשבָֿתָֿא.

parallels.note: “Counsel”: Yahweh's thoughts and counsel stand together.
“Way”: a man's thoughts and his way go together.

phrases.gloss: the form of the thoughts of the heart

words.gloss: reckoning, account, the sum of things
words.summary: Three times, all in Ecclesiastes. BDB's key for it also takes the place name Heshbon, spelled the same, so most of its counted tokens are the city (see the note).

senses.gloss: reckoning, account; the sum of things
senses.definition: The working out of a sum, adding one thing to another; the reasoning that weighs things up.

evidence.note: “Adding one to one to find the reckoning (חֶשְׁבּוֹן).”
“To know, to search out and to seek wisdom and the reckoning”: with חָכְמָה.
“There is no work or reckoning or knowledge or wisdom in the grave, where you are going.”

words.summary: Eight times, always the band of the ephod, “of the same work” as the ephod, which is “the work of a designer (חֹשֵׁב)”. The name is the designer's woven work; Punic ḥšb “weaver” supports the link.

senses.gloss: the woven band of the ephod
senses.definition: The band, woven in one piece with the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet and fine linen, by which it was girded on the high priest.

evidence.note: “The band (חֵשֶׁב) of its ephod which is on it shall be of the same work, of one piece with it”, and the ephod is “the work of a designer (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב)” (Exo 28:6).
“Gird him with the band of the ephod.”
“He girded him with the band of the ephod and bound it to him with it.”

words.summary: Twice, plural: Uzziah's engines of war, and the many schemes men have sought out.

senses.definition: A thing worked out by ingenuity: an engine of war; and the schemes of men set against the uprightness in which God made them.

evidence.note: “He made in Jerusalem devices (חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת), the invention of an inventor, to be on the towers … to shoot arrows and great stones.”
“God made man upright (יָשָׁר), but they have sought out many schemes.”

opposites.note: Man was made upright; his schemes are his own.

words.summary: Once in Daniel's Aramaic, the passive participle.

senses.definition: To be counted as something, as the Hebrew niphal.

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar: “All the dwellers of the earth are reckoned as nothing (כְּלָה חֲשִׁיבִין), and he does according to his will in the army of heaven”, as Isa 40:17 says of the nations in Hebrew.

words.gloss: reckon, count, impute; (ethpeel) be reckoned; (ethpaal) think, reason
words.summary: The Peshitta's verb of the root, for λογίζομαι and διαλογίζομαι. In Romans 4 it carries Gen 15:6 and Psa 32:2 in the same root as the Hebrew, so that Paul's argument reads in the words of the verses he expounds.

senses.definition: To count up, to count a thing as something, and to set righteousness or sin to someone's account.

evidence.note: “The blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness (חָשֵבֿ לֵה זַדִּיקֻותָֿא) without works.”
“Blessed is the man to whom God does not reckon (לָא נֵחשֻובֿ) his sin”: Psa 32:2.
“Not reckoning (ולָא חשַבֿ) to them their sins.”
“Reckon yourselves (חשֻובֿו נַפֿשכֻֿון) to be dead to sin and alive to God.”
“Does he not first sit down and count (חָשֵבֿ) the cost?”
“I count all things loss.”
“Let him who has understanding count the number of the beast.”

senses.definition: To be counted as something, or set to someone's account.

evidence.note: “Abraham believed God, וֵאתֿחַשבַּתֿ לֵה לזַדִּיקֻו”: Gen 15:6.
“To him who works the wage is not reckoned as grace but as debt.”
“We are reckoned as sheep for slaughter (וֵאתֿחשֵבֿנ)”: Psa 44:23.
“He was reckoned (אֵתֿחשֵבֿ) with the lawless”, for Isa 53:12, whose Hebrew is נִמְנָה.

senses.definition: To turn a matter over in the mind or among oneselves.

evidence.note: Mary “was considering (מֵתֿחַשבָֿא הוָתֿ) what this greeting might be” (διελογίζετο).
The rich man “reasoned within himself, What shall I do?”

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for the thoughts of the heart, for διαλογισμός, ἐνθύμησις and λογισμός.

senses.definition: What the heart thinks: evil thoughts, which come from within, and the counsels of hearts that God will judge.

evidence.note: “Out of the heart come evil thoughts (מַחשבָֿתָֿא בִּישָתָֿא), murder, adultery …”
“The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain”: Psa 94:11, the Hebrew מַחְשְׁבוֹת.
The Lord at his coming “will reveal the thoughts of the hearts”.
The word of God is “a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for a settling of accounts, where the Greek has λόγος.

senses.definition: An account to be given or settled, by servants to their master, and by those who watch over others.

evidence.note: A king “who wished to take a reckoning (חֻושבָּנָא) from his servants”.
“Give me the account (חֻושבָּנָא) of your stewardship.”
The master of the talents “came and took account from them”.
Those who watch for your souls “as men who will give their account”.

cognates.gloss: number, count, reckon, compute; (ḥasiba) think, suppose; (ḥāsaba) reckon with, call to account; (ḥisāb) reckoning, account
cognates.note: Both sides of the Hebrew: counting and accounting, and thinking a thing to be so (ḥasiba takes two objects, as חָשַׁב with לְ, Gen 38:15). يَوْمُ الحِسَابِ “the day of reckoning” is the final judgment. Arabic shows ḥ (ح, not خ ḫ) behind ח, and s, the regular Arabic answer to š (not ث ṯ), behind ש.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 564, art. حسب, حَسَبَهُ (n7936)
evidence.note: “He numbered, counted, reckoned, calculated, or computed, it”; and, of the verb of the other measure, “حَسِبَ ‘he thought,’ or … حَسَبَ ‘he reckoned’”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 565, art. حسب, حاسبهُ (n7938)
evidence.note: “He reckoned with him. … He called him to account for it.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 567, art. حسب, حِسَابٌ (n7949)
evidence.note: “A numbering, counting, reckoning, calculation, or computation … يَوْمُ الحِسَابِ [The day of reckoning; i.e., of the final judgment].”

cognates.gloss: think, plan; (pael) plan, count, calculate; (ithpeel) be planned, be considered, valued; (passive participle) esteemed
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud, used where the Hebrew has חָשַׁב in each of its senses: plan (Targ. Gen 50:20), calculate (Targ. Onkelos Lev 25:27), be reckoned (Targ. Lev 17:4). Aramaic ש, not ת, shows š behind ש.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֲשֵׁב (ch.), citing Targ. Gen. L, 20; Targ. Esth. VIII, 3; Pa. Targ. O. Lev. XXV, 27; Ithpe. Targ. Lev. XVII, 4; part. pass. חָשִׁיב “esteemed”

cognates.gloss: think, reckon, deliberate; thought, idea, reckoning; reckoning, calculation, account; thought, reasoning, counsel
cognates.note: The Syriac of the Peshitta, whose words of the root are words of this entry. Syriac ܫ, not ܬ, shows š behind ש.

evidence.locator: root 693 KWB; lexemes 1170 KOWBA (reckoning; thought; idea), 1171 KOWBNA (reckoning; calculation; account), 1172 KWB (think; reckon; deliberate), 1173 MKWBTA (thought; reasoning; counsel)

cognates.gloss: (qal) impute something to someone; (piel) count money; (mḥšb) accountant, treasurer; pl. the exchequer
cognates.note: Neo-Punic “a king to whom excellence is imputed” (KAI 161) is the Hebrew's reckoning to someone's account; the piel participle is the accountant of a sodality (KAI 160) and, in the plural, the government's treasury (RCL 1966).

Punic “Baalhanno the weaver (hḥšb)” (CIS i 74), the noun matching the Hebrew participle חֹשֵׁב of the tabernacle's patterned weaving. That the same root names the reckoner and the weaver of patterns supports keeping the craft sense and חֵשֶׁב under this root.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ḥošeb] n.m. WEAVER.”

cognates.note: Listed by Anderson and Moser under Proto-Semitic *ḥšb “compute”; not in Oracc's glossaries and not checked in CAD. Akkadian lost *ḥ, so a word spelled with h may be a late borrowing from Aramaic. Possible only; it counts neither way.

evidence.locator: SEM001003 ḥšb [compute] V, AKK003570 hašābu [count] V

doctrine.statement: When Yahweh brought Abram outside and promised him a seed like the stars, and in the same speech the land (Gen 15:5, 7), “he believed in Yahweh, and he reckoned it to him as righteousness” (Gen 15:6). The verb is the reckoner's: what is reckoned to a man is set to his account, as an offering is reckoned to the one who brings it, or blood to the man who sheds it (Lev 7:18; 17:4; Num 18:27). It works the other way too: “blessed is the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon iniquity” (Psa 32:2), and Shimei begs David, “let not my lord reckon iniquity to me, and do not remember” (2Sa 19:20). Phinehas's zeal “was reckoned to him as righteousness to all generations” (Psa 106:31). Paul sets Gen 15:6 beside Psa 32:1–2: righteousness is reckoned to the one who believes, not paid as a wage to the one who works, and it was reckoned to Abraham before he was circumcised, so that he is the father of all who believe (Rom 4:3–11); it was written “not for his sake alone, but for us also, to whom it will be reckoned, who believe on him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead” (Rom 4:23–24). The promise Abraham believed was that he should be “heir of the world” (Rom 4:13), the land he walked through and never received (Gen 13:15, 17; Act 7:5), dying in faith not having received the promises (Heb 11:8–13). Those who are of faith are Abraham's sons and, being Christ's, heirs according to the promise (Gal 3:6–9, 29); James adds that the faith reckoned to him was completed by his works when he offered Isaac (Jas 2:21–23). God was in Christ “not reckoning to them their trespasses” (2Co 5:19). From the verses: God sets righteousness to the account of the one who believes his promise, the promise to Abraham of the land and the seed, and does not set to his account the sins he forgives; the faith that is reckoned is a faith that obeys.

Before the flood “Yahweh saw that the evil of man was great in the earth, and every form of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day” (Gen 6:5). Yahweh “knows the thoughts of man, that they are vapour” (Psa 94:11); he searches all hearts and understands every form of the thoughts (1Ch 28:9); and he calls the wicked to forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts and return to him, for “my thoughts are not your thoughts” (Isa 55:7–9). Jerusalem is told, “wash your heart from evil … how long will your thoughts of iniquity lodge within you?” (Jer 4:14). Jesus says, “out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries … these are what defile the man” (Mat 15:19–20), and “all these evil things come from within” (Mrk 7:21–23). Paul applies Psa 94:11 to the reasonings of the wise (1Co 3:20); the word of God discerns “the thoughts and intents of the heart” (Heb 4:12); and the Lord at his coming “will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the hearts” (1Co 4:5). From the verses: the source of sin is man's own heart and its thoughts; scripture places it within him, not in a being outside him, and the way out is to forsake those thoughts for Yahweh's and to be searched by his word, as all will be at Christ's return.

Joseph tells his brothers, “you planned evil against me; God planned it for good, to do as it is this day, to keep many people alive” (Gen 50:20). “Many are the plans in a man's heart, but the counsel of Yahweh, that will stand” (Pro 19:21); “a man's heart plans his way, but Yahweh establishes his step” (Pro 16:9); Yahweh brings the counsel of the nations to nothing, but “the counsel of Yahweh stands for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations” (Psa 33:10–11). To the exiles in Babylon: “when seventy years are completed … I will bring you back to this place; for I know the thoughts that I think toward you … thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope” (Jer 29:10–11). The nations gathered against Zion “do not know the thoughts of Yahweh … for he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor” (Mic 4:11–12), in the chapter where the law goes out from Zion and “Yahweh will reign over them in Mount Zion from now and for ever” (Mic 4:2, 7). Yahweh also “devises means so that the banished one is not cast out from him” (2Sa 14:14). From the verses: men plan, but Yahweh's purpose stands and turns their evil plans to its end; that purpose is the return of his people to their land and his reign from Zion.

Qoheleth says, “whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength, for there is no work or reckoning (חֶשְׁבּוֹן) or knowledge or wisdom in the grave, where you are going” (Ecc 9:10), and “the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing” (Ecc 9:5). The psalmist near death says, “I am reckoned with those who go down to the pit … like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more”, and asks, “will you work wonders for the dead? … will your lovingkindness be declared in the grave?” (Psa 88:5–6, 11–12). Of man “whose breath is in his nostrils” Isaiah asks, “at what is he to be reckoned?” (Isa 2:22). From the verses: in death there is no thought, reckoning or knowledge; the dead do not go on thinking in another state. The hope scripture gives is resurrection: those who “sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake” (Dan 12:2), and those “who fear Yahweh and esteem his name” are written in a book of remembrance before him, to be his “in the day that I make” (Mal 3:16–17).

Of Yahweh's servant: “He was despised and forsaken of men … and we did not esteem him (לֹא חֲשַׁבְנֻהוּ). Surely he has borne our sicknesses and carried our pains; yet we reckoned him (חֲשַׁבְנֻהוּ) stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted. But he was pierced for our transgressions” (Isa 53:3–5). Matthew applies Isa 53:4 to Jesus (Mat 8:17); Philip, from Isa 53:7–8, “preached to him Jesus” (Act 8:32–35); Peter writes, “by whose stripes you were healed” (1Pe 2:24). In the Peshitta, Mrk 15:28, “he was reckoned (אֵתֿחשֵבֿ) with the lawless”, renders Isa 53:12. From the verses: men reckoned the servant a man under God's judgment for his own sin; what he bore was theirs, and he was then exalted (Isa 52:13; 53:12).

BDB keys: h.gr.aa verb, h.gr.ak מַחֲשָׁבָה, h.gr.ae חֶשְׁבּוֹן, h.gr.ab חֵשֶׁב, h.gr.ag חִשָּׁבוֹן, xh.ap.aa Aramaic חֲשַׁב; names in names/: h.gr.ah hashabiah, h.gr.ad hasshub, h.gr.ac hashubah, h.gr.aj hashabneiah, h.gr.ai hashabnah. Left unassigned: h.gr.af, the city Heshbon (41 tokens; a place name, not a personal name, so no name file; whether the city is named from the root, “reckoning”, is not shown by any verse); h.gr.al חַשְׁבַּדָּנָה Hashbaddanah (Neh 8:4), whose first element looks like חשב but whose second is not clear, so no name file yet; m.bq.ai, a zero-token cross-reference for מַחֲשֶׁבֶת. Shared tokens: the brief counts 24 of h.gr.ae's 27 tokens under both the noun and the city; only Ecc 7:25, 7:27 and 9:10 are the noun, so lexicon-support's use count for חֶשְׁבּוֹן is inflated. The Peshitta's words (verb חשַבֿ with peal, ethpeel and ethpaal; מַחשַבֿתָּא; חֻושבָּנָא) are entered with stems from SEDRA's form codes; no pael occurs. חֻושָבָֿא (Jas 3:15, lexeme 1170) is not entered. Greek: the brief's “loan” διαλογισμός is a false lead (Thayer says only that the Septuagint uses it for מַחֲשָׁבָה); recorded as a rendering. Leads not followed: Ge'ez ḥasaba “count, reckon” (Dillmann, Leslau; not checked by page); Ugaritic ḥšb/ḥtbn “account” (DULAT, not vendored; would show whether ש is š or ṯ there, though Arabic س and Syriac ܫ already show š); Old South Arabian (Biella has no ḤSB entry found by search); Akkadian hašābu in CAD; Egyptian ḥsb “count, reckon” (Wiktionary compares it; TLA's ḥsb entries in the brief are “break”, “fracture”, so the Egyptian “count” verb was not found in the vendored TLA; not Semitic and not a loan, so not recorded). Open questions: (1) whether the craft sense (חֹשֵׁב designer/weaver, חֵשֶׁב the woven band) is “devising” patterns or an older weaving root that fell together with “reckon”; Punic has both ḥšb “impute” and ḥšb “weaver”, and nothing shows two sounds behind any letter, so they are kept as one; (2) Psa 140:3, 140:5 and Ezk 38:10 are tagged qal plan; (3) the doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
